Central Nervous System
Physiology
Ascending Tracts

Quick Overview

Ascending tracts carry sensory information from the spinal cord up to higher centers of the CNS. This lesson covers what happens to sensory fibers entering the spinal cord, the shared organizational rules of ascending tracts (three-neuron chains, dorsal root ganglion origin, crossing, and thalamic relay), and the classification of the three major ascending systems — the anterolateral spinothalamic tracts, the posterior/dorsal column system, and the tracts carrying unconscious proprioception. It also covers the sensory lemnisci, the crossed second-order fiber bundles that carry these signals through the brainstem to the thalamus.

Complete Lesson Content

Fate of Sensory Fibers Entering the Spinal Cord

Sensory fibers entering the spinal cord via the dorsal roots can do one of three things:

  1. Elicit local spinal reflexes (e.g., flexion withdrawal reflex).
  2. Produce an autonomic reflex (e.g., urinary bladder contraction).
  3. Ascend and reach higher levels of the CNS via ascending tracts.

Definition and Shared Characters of Ascending Tracts

Definition: An ascending tract is a group of sensation-carrying fibers that ascend in the spinal cord.

Characters shared by all ascending tracts:

1. All are formed of three-order neurons.
2. The first-order neurons of every ascending tract are the dorsal root ganglion cells.
3. Most of the axons of the second-order neurons cross to the opposite side — so most conscious sensations from the left side of the body reach the right sensory cortex, and vice versa.
4. All sensations relay in the thalamus before reaching the cortex, except smell and unconscious proprioceptive sensations.

Classification into Three Major Systems

The most important ascending tracts are classified into three major systems, based on the type of sensation each carries:

1. Anterolateral Spinothalamic Tracts

Carry pain, temperature, pressure, and crude touch. They include:

  • Ventral (anterior) spinothalamic tract: carries crude (light) touch.
  • Lateral spinothalamic tract: carries pain, temperature, muscle fatigue, and sex orgasm.

2. Posterior (Dorsal) Column System — Gracile & Cuneate Tracts

Carries conscious proprioceptive sensations, stereognosis, vibration sense, tactile localization, and tactile discrimination.

3. Tracts Carrying Unconscious Proprioceptive Sensations

Include the dorsal and ventral spino-cerebellar tracts, the spino-reticular tract, and the spino-olivary tract.

Sensory Lemnisci

The sensory lemnisci are the pathways of the sensory ascending tracts within the brainstem. Each lemniscus is formed of the axons of the second-order neurons after they have crossed to the opposite side.

Lemniscus Origin Course / Termination
Spinal lemniscus Combination of the lateral and ventral spinothalamic tracts. Gives collaterals to the reticular formation; ends in the ventro-postrolateral nucleus of the thalamus (PVLNT).
Medial lemniscus Axons of the gracile and cuneate nuclei (both sides) cross to form the internal arcuate fibers; their decussation forms the sensory decussation. Ascends as the medial lemniscus, giving collaterals to the reticular formation and cerebellum (external arcuate fibers); ends in PVLNT of both sides.
Trigeminal lemniscus Axons of the main sensory nuclei of the trigeminal nerve, in the pons and spinal cord. Terminates in the posterior medial ventral nucleus of the thalamus (PVMNT).
Lateral lemniscus Axons of the dorsal and ventral cochlear nuclei (2nd-order neurons of the hearing pathway). Ascends to terminate in the inferior colliculi of the midbrain.

Key Points / Quick Review

Fate of dorsal root fibers

  • Local spinal reflex
  • Autonomic reflex
  • Ascend via ascending tracts

Shared rules of ascending tracts

  • 3-neuron chain
  • 1st-order = dorsal root ganglion cells
  • Most 2nd-order axons cross
  • All relay in thalamus except smell & unconscious proprioception

Anterolateral spinothalamic system

  • Ventral tract → crude touch
  • Lateral tract → pain, temperature, muscle fatigue, orgasm

Dorsal column system

  • Gracile & cuneate tracts
  • Conscious proprioception, stereognosis, vibration, tactile localization & discrimination

Unconscious proprioceptive tracts

  • Dorsal & ventral spinocerebellar
  • Spino-reticular
  • Spino-olivary

Sensory lemnisci — key destinations

  • Spinal lemniscus → PVLNT
  • Medial lemniscus → PVLNT (crosses as internal arcuate fibers)
  • Trigeminal lemniscus → PVMNT
  • Lateral lemniscus → inferior colliculi
